question: Using the index level and VIX shown, and the square-root-of-time rule (12 months per year), what is the approximate one-standard-deviation expected move over the next month?
Under the normal-distribution assumption, roughly what share of the time should the index finish the month inside the one-standard-deviation band shown, and what is the main caveat?
options: About 68%; real returns have fatter tails, so large moves occur more often than predicted
About 95%; the band is a two-standard-deviation band
About 50%, because VIX measures the median expected move
About 68%, and because VIX is a forward-looking estimate the normal model tends to overstate large moves
